intro.text: In the Exchange Variation White gives up the Spanish bishop to damage Black's pawn structure. The play revolves around White's healthy kingside majority against Black's bishop pair and quick development.

White gives up the Spanish bishop at once to change the pawn structure. Black gets the bishop pair and fast development; White gets a healthy kingside pawn majority that can become decisive in an endgame.
Black recaptures towards the centre, opening lines for the queen and light-squared bishop. White now has the healthy kingside majority; Black has the bishop pair and fast development.
White castles and keeps the option of opening the centre. Black usually protects the centre pawn and develops quickly to make the bishop pair count before the endgame.
